title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page for Grothendieck's 1970 programme on Barsotti–Tate groups and Dieudonné crystals (Montréal lectures; ICM Nice talk). The left and right columns contain three separate computations; most of the text concerns the first.

(1) Setup. M is the Dieudonné crystal of a truncated BT group (probably a BT_1) over a base S of characteristic p, on the crystalline site. φ: X_cris → X_zar is the projection to the Zariski topos. M carries F and V. From them he forms the kernel, image and cokernel pieces _F M, _p M, _V M, M_F, M_p, M_V. These fit into a six-term exact sequence
0 → _F M~ → _p M~ →F _V M → M_p →V M_p~ → M_V~ → 0.
An isomorphism Θ (a Cartier/Frobenius-linear identification) links the middle terms. The triangle M_{/F} → M_{/p} → M_{/V} is the crystalline version of the familiar facts Ker F = Im V and Im F = Ker V, with F inducing an isomorphism between Frobenius twists of graded pieces.

(2) Key observation: M_{/p} = φ*(Δ(M)). The piece M_{/p} is pulled back from a Zariski object Δ(M). This is justified by the computation on the upper right. For a PD-thickening J ⊂ B → A in characteristic p (λ ↦ λ^p), x^p = p!·γ_p(x) = 0 for x ∈ J. So Frobenius kills J and factors through B/J^{(p)}B and through A. Hence a Frobenius-pulled-back crystal depends only on its Zariski value. This is the standard fact that Frob* of a crystal mod p is a Zariski object. The sketch J^{(p)}B, I ⊂ C → A, B ⊗ B → A compares two thickenings through a common one.

(3) Zariski data. On S_zar, Δ(M) is a two-term complex [t* → ω] with cohomology H_1* and H_0. This is the co-Lie (Lie) complex data, written as the six-term sequence
0 → n → D_1 → t* → ω → D_0 → ν* → 0.
He then splits off pieces 0 → n → D_1 → D~_1 → 0 and 0 → D~_0 → D_0 → ν* → 0, which are 'uniquely determined by I(M)'. This leaves:
(i) a four-term exact sequence 0 → D~_1 → t* → ω → D~_0 → 0; and
(ii) a triangle t*[1] → ω → Δ~(M), in which ω is 'known'.
The aim, after crossing out the weaker option (a) 'descend M_{/F} and M_{/V}', is (b) 'descend the whole triangle' from cris to zar. Concretely, Θ is to descend to a Zariski ϑ, and one must construct the isomorphisms [t* → ω] ≃ Δ~(M) that are compatible after φ*.

(4) Deformation-theoretic bookkeeping. He records the choices as relative Ext groups for the morphism of topoi S_zar 'mod' S_cris, with coefficients (D~_0, D~_1):
- automorphisms in Ext^0 = 0 (with an exclamation mark);
- arbitrariness (choices of isomorphisms, i.e. extension classes) in Ext^1;
- obstructions in Ext^2.
This is the standard trichotomy, applied to relative cohomology of φ.

(5) Descent diagram (bottom right). A simplicial descent diagram X~ ⇐ X×X ≡ X×X×X over S, with flat vertical maps and an F_S arrow. This is fpqc or Frobenius descent of the thickened object (X~ over X, Y×X) to make the construction functorial.

Overall purpose: describe a BT_1 (or its Dieudonné crystal) by Zariski-level linear algebra. That means Hodge and conjugate pieces together with Frobenius-linear identifications, controlled by the co-Lie complex, over a non-reduced, non-smooth base.
errors: Not an error but a gap: the claim that the pieces n, ν*, D~_0, D~_1 are 'uniquely determined by I(M)' is asserted without argument; I(M) is not defined on the page.

The vanishing Ext^0(S_zar mod S_cris; D~_0, D~_1) = 0 is asserted with an exclamation mark but not justified. It is plausible because the coefficients sit in different degrees, or because Frobenius is nilpotent on the relevant pieces.
Sign and indexing of the six-term F/V sequence are hard to read in the image. The middle term may be M_{/p} rather than M_F, so the exactness as transcribed cannot be fully checked.

ideas.what: Frobenius pullback of a crystal in characteristic p depends only on its Zariski value, because Frobenius on a PD-thickening B kills J (x^p = p!γ_p(x)) and factors through B/J; hence M_{/p} = φ*(Δ(M))

ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (1974)

missed.claim: Around 1970 Grothendieck was trying to descend the full F/V triangle of the Dieudonné crystal of a BT_1 from the crystalline to the Zariski topos. The resulting Zariski datum is pieces of the co-Lie complex plus a Frobenius-linear identification ϑ. This anticipates the 'F-zip' description of BT_1's (Kraft, Moonen–Wedhorn) over arbitrary characteristic-p bases. It also anticipates the later truncated-display and Dieudonné-display approaches of Lau and Zink, which likewise turn crystalline data into Zariski linear algebra. Here, unusually, the non-smooth case is included, with the extra terms n and ν* from the Lie complex.
missed.quote: b) descendre le triangle tout entier ... On descend Θ en ϑ ... M_{/p} = φ*(Δ(M))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests an F-zip-type invariant for BT_1 over non-smooth or non-reduced bases built from the co-Lie complex. Such a refined invariant is not standard in the literature.

missed.claim: He sets up a deformation-theoretic control of the choices: the isomorphisms [t* → ω] ≃ Δ~(M) are rigid (Ext^0 = 0), the choices form a torsor under Ext^1, and the obstructions lie in Ext^2, all relative to S_zar → S_cris. The computation of these relative Ext groups, and hence of when a Zariski model exists, is left open.
missed.quote: l'arbitraire est dans ... Ext^1(S_zar mod S_cris; D~_0, D~_1) ; les automorphismes ... Ext^0(...)=0 ! Obstruction ... dans Ext^2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relative cohomology of the projection cris → zar is now accessible via derived de Rham and prismatic methods. Such a computation could make this classification statement precise.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients — Frobenius pullback of crystals being Zariski, F/V exact sequences, and co-Lie complexes — are known and partly due to Grothendieck. The specific plan is less standard: descending the whole F/V triangle to a Zariski datum controlled by relative Ext groups, in effect an F-zip over non-smooth bases. But it is fragmentary and unproved.
transcription_corrections: 'les obstructions à le [?] structure [?] sont Ext^0(...)=0' should most likely read 'les automorphismes de la structure sont dans Ext^0(...) = 0 !'. The obstruction is the separate final line, in Ext^2.
The label under 'I ⊂ C' reads 'r.d.' rather than 'n.d.'; its meaning is unclear.
In the F/V six-term sequence, the term after _V M appears as M_{/p} (with Θ above it) rather than M_F; the reading is uncertain.
'i.e. on doit considérer les isom.' — the inserted word above the struck-out 'donner' looks like 'construire' or 'considérer'.
'descendant ... par φ*' is probably 'descendant [les isomorphismes] connus par φ* de Δ~(M)'.
